title: Robin Li Warns of AI Bubble Risk: Massive Investment in Computing Power, Application Deployment Still Falling Short of Expectations

content_html:
Robin Li, Chairman and CEO of Baidu Group, said on November 17 at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit that the AI industry is currently investing heavily in computing power and infrastructure, but the real-world deployment of upper-layer applications has yet to meet expectations. If the application layer fails to make breakthroughs over the long term, the industry may face the risk of an AI bubble.

During the panel discussion “Building an Open and Inclusive AI Innovation Ecosystem,” Li pointed out that the AI technology stack includes not only chips, cloud, models, and applications, but also requires supporting organizational capabilities above the application layer. Using the electricity revolution as an example, he said that advanced technology alone is not enough to unlock economic value; corresponding organizational change is also needed to drive productivity gains.

Although he warned of bubble risks in the industry, Li remains optimistic about AI’s long-term development and said that the share of Baidu’s revenue coming from AI businesses will continue to rise in the future.

Earlier, at Baidu World 2026 on November 12, Li proposed the concept of the “intelligent organization,” arguing that if AI is the electricity of a new era, then the intelligent organization is the new factory of the AI era. Only by deeply integrating AI capabilities with organizational methods can productivity truly be unleashed.

Li’s views extend the focus of competition in the AI industry from computing power and model capabilities further to application deployment and organizational change, while also highlighting that realizing AI’s commercial value still faces real-world challenges.
